research_question: In people hospitalised with acute stroke, do multifaceted implementation interventions (e.g. education, audit and feedback, local champions, protocols/clinical pathways, with or without care-delivery redesign), compared with no implementation intervention or usual practice, increase adherence to evidence-based recommended processes of care during the hospital admission?
treatment_label: Multifaceted implementation intervention (education, audit and feedback, champions, protocols/pathways, ± care-delivery change)
control_label: No implementation intervention / usual care or practice as normal
outcome_description: Proportion of patients (or eligible patients) who received the recommended process of care — the trial's primary adherence or quality-of-care process measure (e.g. proportion of eligible patients given thrombolysis, proportion managed per a defined care protocol, proportion receiving dysphagia screening or prophylaxis) — extracted as number adherent (events) out of number of patients in each arm (total) during the follow-up/post-intervention period at the end of the intervention. Patient-level numbers, not hospitals or clusters. Cluster trials: use reported cluster-adjusted RR/OR with CI where available (convert CI to SE of log RR; convert OR to RR only if baseline risk given), otherwise inflate the SE by the design effect 1 + (average cluster size − 1) × ICC using the trial's ICC or an assumed ICC of 0.05.
positive_direction: A positive effect (RR > 1 / positive Hedges g) means patients in the multifaceted implementation intervention arm were MORE likely to receive the recommended evidence-based process of care than patients in the usual-practice control arm.
search_queries: multifaceted implementation intervention acute stroke care adherence cluster randomised trial
quality improvement intervention stroke guideline adherence thrombolysis rates controlled trial
audit and feedback education protocol stroke unit evidence-based care processes randomized effect
inclusion_criteria: Randomised or cluster-randomised trial conducted in an acute stroke / acute hospital stroke care setting
Evaluates a multifaceted implementation, quality-improvement or knowledge-translation intervention against no implementation intervention or usual practice
Reports some quantitative measure of adherence to a recommended process of care during the hospital admission (counts, proportions, or an adjusted effect estimate with CI)
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, editorial, commentary, opinion or purely theoretical/protocol paper)

No comparison between an implementation intervention and a no-intervention/usual-practice control (including trials whose control arm receives another active implementation strategy, and uncontrolled before-and-after studies)
No quantitative outcome data from which an effect size can be computed (no events/totals, proportions, or effect estimate with CI/SE)

Unrelated to the research topic (non-stroke conditions, single-component interventions only, post-discharge/community adherence only, or reporting only patient clinical outcomes, costs, staff knowledge or satisfaction)
moderators_to_extract: Number and type of intervention components (e.g. education only + audit vs including care-delivery change)
Specific process measure used (thrombolysis, dysphagia screening, protocol adherence, composite)
Number of clusters and average cluster size (sample size category)
Risk of bias / baseline adherence rate in control arm
effect_size_note: Pool as risk ratio (intervention/control) using a random-effects model on the log risk ratio (DerSimonian–Laird or REML, with Hartung–Knapp adjustment considered given few trials). RR > 1 favours the intervention. For cluster-randomised trials, prefer the paper's cluster-adjusted RR/OR with CI (convert CI to SE of log RR; convert OR to RR only when baseline risk is reported); otherwise inflate the naive SE by sqrt(design effect) with design effect = 1 + (mean cluster size − 1) × ICC, using the trial-reported ICC or an explicitly stated assumed ICC of 0.05. Multi-arm trials: combine intervention arms into a single multifaceted arm versus control. Use post-intervention period data only for before-after designs within randomised trials.
single_outcome_target: Adherence to evidence-based recommended processes of acute stroke care
